resources.string: The app ran into an unexpected error and needs to close. The log below may help explain what happened.

Scalara changes your device\'s display resolution without root, using the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS system permission and the same WindowManager mechanism behind \"adb shell wm size\". This permission cannot be granted through a normal permission prompt \u2014 it has to be granted once via ADB, or managed through Shizuku, before Scalara can do anything.

WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS lets an app modify secure system settings, not just display resolution. Scalara only uses it to change resolution and density, but you\'re trusting Scalara with a permission that could, in principle, affect other system settings.\n\nSetting an unusual resolution can make some apps render incorrectly, make on-screen text or controls hard to read, or in rare cases make the screen difficult to navigate until the resolution is reset. If that happens, you can usually recover by reconnecting ADB and running the reset command, or via Settings on devices that expose a display size option.
Scalara is an independent, open-source project. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or supported by Google or your device manufacturer.

By tapping \"I understand and agree\", you confirm that you\'ve read the above, understand the risks of granting WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS, and agree to proceed at your own responsibility. This screen only appears once, the first time Scalara is installed.
Scroll to the bottom to continue
Choose how to grant the permission
Scalara needs WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS to change your display resolution. Pick one of the two supported methods below.
Grant the permission once from a computer using a single ADB command. The permission then stays granted permanently \u2014 Scalara will not contact Shizuku at all.
Let the Shizuku app manage the permission for you. No computer needed after Shizuku itself is running, but Scalara depends on the Shizuku service staying active.

1. Connect this device to a computer with ADB installed, with USB debugging enabled.
2. Open a terminal on that computer.
3. Run the command below.
4. Come back here and tap "Verify permission".
Once granted this way, the permission is treated as permanent. Scalara will not request the Shizuku binder or ask you to install Shizuku.
Permission not detected yet. Run the command above, then try again.
1. Install Shizuku if you haven\'t already.\n2. Start the Shizuku service from the Shizuku app (via ADB pairing or root, depending on your device).\n3. Come back here and tap \"Request permission\".
Shizuku is running \u2014 permission not granted yet
Shizuku is running and permission is granted
Permission was denied with \"don\'t ask again\". Grant it from the Shizuku app\'s own screen instead.
The WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission was detected. Scalara will treat this as permanent.
The permission is granted through Shizuku. Keep the Shizuku service running so Scalara continues to work.
Scalara no longer has the WRITE_SECURE_SETTINGS permission. It may have been revoked by the system or another app. You\'ll need to go through setup again.
Scalara can no longer reach Shizuku, or the permission was revoked. Make sure the Shizuku service is running, then go through setup again.
